title: private-deploy networking incident - vpc peering / dns / tls / egress debugging
content:
Summary:
- Scratchpad for the networking incident affecting customer X private deployment (reported 2024-11-02 03:10 UTC).
- User-facing symptom: requests to hosted model endpoints time out or return TLS errors from services inside customer VPC when trying to call out to Redwood public metadata endpoints / model registry.
- Affects: control-plane sync and scheduled model downloads; inference itself degraded on new cold starts.

Timeline / quick notes:
- 2024-11-02 03:06 UTC: customer reported intermittent TLS handshake failures from worker nodes when contacting api.redwood-inference.com (via NAT).
- 03:12: initial suspicion: NAT gateway flapping / route table change after maintenance window.
- 03:28: reproduced from bastion (customer VPC) -> TLS handshake times out. From same subnet an instance can curl other public endpoints successfully.
- 04:01: created this doc with commands and logs.

What I tried (commands + immediate observations):
- Basic DNS/resolve checks from customer bastion:
  $ dig +short api.redwood-inference.com
  34.212.45.121
  (resolves to public IP)

- Verify can reach IP (ICMP / tcp):
  $ ping -c3 34.212.45.121
  PING 34.212.45.121 (34.212.45.121): 56 data bytes
  --- 34.212.45.121 ping statistics ---
  3 packets transmitted, 0 packets received, 100% packet loss
  => ICMP blocked (not conclusive)

  $ traceroute -n 34.212.45.121
  1  10.0.1.1  0.4 ms
  2  10.0.0.1  1.2 ms
  3  52.95.128.1  9.1 ms
  4  * * *
  => drops after customer edge (possible egress filter / firewall)

- TLS handshake debug (openssl s_client):
  $ openssl s_client -connect api.redwood-inference.com:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.com -timeout 5
  CONNECTED(00000003)
  139695... handshake timeout
  write:errno=110
  => TCP connects intermittently but TLS fails/timeout

- cURL with verbose to capture TCP/TLS state:
  $ curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.com/health
  * TCP_NODELAY set
  * Connected to api.redwood-inference.com (34.212.45.121) port 443 (#0)
  * TLS 1.2 connection using ???
  * SSL connection error: "SSL: certificate verify failed" (sometimes)
  * Operation timed out after 5001 milliseconds
  => mixed results across attempts (sometimes verify error, sometimes timeout)

- From an external (control) host (our office VPN) same curl succeeds immediately, cert chain looks good. So issue appears customer-side egress/mitm or path MTU / fragment loss.

- Check iptables / host firewall on worker node: no OUTPUT rules blocking 443.
- Check VPC route table: default route to NAT gateway present for private subnets.
- Check NAT gateway CloudWatch metrics: active, no high error rate.
- Check security groups on instances: outbound 0.0.0.0/0:443 allowed.

- AWS VPC peering / Transit/Route table checks (customer-managed):
  $ aws ec2 describe-vpc-peering-connections --filters Name=status-code,Values=active
  -> peering active between prod-vpc and central-services-vpc
  BUT peering does not provide internet access across VPCs; ensure NAT/IGW in correct VPC.

- DNS special cases: customer uses split-horizon DNS with conditional forwarding to internal resolvers.
  $ nslookup api.redwood-inference.com <internal-dns-server>
  Server: internal-dns
  Name: api.redwood-inference.com
  Address: 34.212.45.121
  => resolves to public IP (no internal nat-ing)

- MTU suspicion: path MTU mismatch causing TLS fragments to drop. Test with curl --max-filesize or set MTU lower:
  $ ping -M do -s 1420 34.212.45.121
  packet too big
  => need binary search MTU. I set eth0 mtu to 1400 temporarily and TLS handshake succeeded once.
  => strong indicator of MTU/fragmentation problem on the path (maybe a firewall dropping fragments)

- Observed intermittent x509 errors on some nodes: "x509: certificate signed by unknown authority"
  - Those nodes have an internal proxy performing TLS interception (corporate security). Need to confirm with customer whether transparent proxy is in use.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Path MTU / fragmentation issue between customer VPC egress and our public IPs, causing TLS handshake packets (SYN+TLS data) to be dropped and timeouts.
2) Transparent TLS interception / corporate proxy rewriting certs for some hosts -> causes verify failures for some nodes.
3) Intermittent NAT gateway / firewall ACL rules periodically dropping long-lived connections or fragments.
4) Route table changes or missing NAT in specific AZs causing egress to blackhole to a firewall.

Evidence for MTU theory:
- Lowering MTU on host temporarily allowed handshake to complete.
- Traceroute shows drop after edge device (likely firewall/edge NAT).

Evidence for proxy theory:
- Some nodes show x509 unknown authority errors; curl -v shows different cert subject on those nodes (subject CN: InternalCorpProxy), confirmed by customer security team for a subset of hosts. This explains cert errors but not the timeouts for nodes without proxy.

What we still need to confirm / next steps:
- (Owner: Samir) Check edge firewall vendor logs (customer) for dropped fragments / ICMP "fragmentation needed" messages in the time window. Ask them to enable ICMP type 3 code 4 logs.
- (Owner: Maya) Validate NAT gateway/subnet mapping across AZs: ensure private subnets route to NAT in same AZ or a functioning NAT gateway. Collect flow logs for the time range.
- (Owner: Harper) Reproduce with controlled MTU test: run iperf3 and controlled TCP handshake with increased MSS to see if fragmentation triggers drops. Capture tcpdump during failing handshake (tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/handshake.pcap port 443).
- (Owner: Noah) Confirm which nodes are behind corporate TLS interception. Map which subnets have proxy config and which do not.

Immediate mitigations to propose to customer:
- If firewall can be configured, allow ICMP "fragmentation needed" through and/or reduce MTU on edge device.
- If proxy is intentional and unavoidable, add our CA / SNI exceptions or configure nodes to trust the proxy CA (temporary).
- As a short-term workaround for model downloads: use an alternative endpoint that supports smaller packets or a CDN edge in their region (we can spin up an S3-backed mirror via signed URL).

Logs / snippets (sanitized):
- tail /var/log/syslog | grep api.redwood
  Nov 02 03:10:27 worker-1 kernel: conntrack: table full, dropping packet
  Nov 02 03:10:27 worker-1 kernel: TCP: refused connect on dev eth0
  => conntrack saturation? might be red herring, but note it.

- openssl s_client output (failing run):
  CONNECTED(00000003)
  139... mix bytes
  write:errno=104
  ---
  no peer certificate available
  ---
  SSL handshake aborted: error:14077410:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:unknown protocol

- curl verbose showing proxy cert (on intercepted node):
  * Server certificate:
  * subject: CN=InternalCorpProxy
  * start date: Nov 01 00:00:00 2024 GMT
  * expire date: Nov 01 00:00:00 2025 GMT
  * issuer: CN=InternalCorpProxy CA

Open questions / unresolved:
- Does customer edge device perform packet reassembly/filtering that drops fragments? (asked network team for config dump)
- Are there differing route tables per AZ? (asked infra team for full dump)
- Is conntrack table saturation on nodes contributing to weird TCP resets? Need netstat -s and conntrack -L at time of incident.

Action items (short):
- [ ] Run tcpdump on failing node during next incident window and share pcap. (Harper)
- [ ] Ask customer to enable ICMP 'fragmentation needed' logs on firewall and share. (Samir)
- [ ] Collect NAT gateway metrics + route table mappings for all private subnets. (Maya)
- [ ] Provide temporary mirror endpoint / S3 signed URL for model downloads. (Engineering ops)
- [ ] If proxy confirmed: document CA install steps for our agents / provide bypass config for model registry endpoints. (Noah)

Notes for postmortem (if confirmed MTU issue):
- Root cause: firewall/edge device dropping IPv4 fragments (or blocking ICMP PMTU messages) resulting in TLS handshake stalls when TLS ServerHello or continuation packets need fragmentation.
- Detection: multiple hosts in subnet experiencing timeouts to public endpoints but not to non-fragmented small-packet endpoints; temporary success after MTU change.
- Mitigation: ensure ICMP PMTU helper passes through, or set MTU lower on host route, or upgrade edge device to reassemble/handle fragments.

Misc references:
- RFC 1191 + path MTU discovery notes (customer network team has these on their firewall vendor guide)
- internal runbook: confluence:private-deploy/vpc-peering-runbook
- Jira ticket: RDW-4821 (incident)

Scratchpad thoughts / hypotheses to keep in mind:
- Could be combination: proxy on some AZs + MTU problem on others -> explains mixed symptoms across nodes.
- conntrack saturations may amplify symptom by dropping fragments or refusing new TCP connections -> ask for increased conntrack table size as temporary measure.

If/when we get pcap: next steps for analysis:
- open in Wireshark, filter "tcp.port==443" and look for repeated retransmissions, DUP ACKs, ICMP type 3 code 4 messages, and patterns where SYN / ACK exchange completes but TLS ClientHello gets no ServerHello.
- confirm MSS values and whether SACK/TS options present.

End of scratchpad.

(Will update as customer/infra teams respond.)
